proof.surface: listener package Go integration test on a nats:2.10 Docker testcontainer: real publishHandler over HTTP -> real core NATS -> real coreNATSDeliveryHandler/roleTopicDelivery -> real bus.Client.RequestCoreTo against a registered, live holder (ses_deaf) with no subscriber on its agent subject. RequestCoreTo uses PublishRequest plus a manual inbox (never nats.Conn.Request), so a subject nobody subscribes to has no ErrNoResponders path and surfaces as nats.ErrTimeout at the deadline — which is why a fresh-but-deaf holder is receipt_timeout.

documentationFeedback: packages/envoy/AGENTS.md is accurate. docs/solutions/architecture-patterns/core-nats-receipt-backed-current-holder-delivery.md has two wording defects the reviewer should weigh (neither changes behaviour): (a) the 'Correct: require the selected receiver to reply' Go snippet (lines 86-93) still maps every RequestCoreTo error to publishDeliveryException(..., "delivery_failed"), contradicting the sentence immediately below it at line 107 ('observable as receipt_timeout (fresh but deaf) and delivery_failed (stopped)') — a reader copying the 'Correct' pattern reproduces the pre-LEGION-108 bug; the snippet needs an errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) -> receipt_timeout branch. (b) line 35's parenthetical 'the receiver has the envelope and has not acknowledged it — a slow holder, not a lost message' overstates: a holder whose session-registry entry is inside ClaimStaleAfter (5 min, internal/session/claim.go:13) but whose process is gone also gets receipt_timeout, and it never had the envelope (RequestCoreTo publishes to a subject with no subscriber and times out). AGENTS.md's phrasing — 'the message was forwarded and not acknowledged; the Legion daemon treats it as delivered to a live process' — is the accurate one and the parent contract (daemon probes on receipt_timeout) covers the dead-but-fresh case.
observations: The implementer's handoff proof was complete and reproduced exactly; every reason assertion in the four line-2 tests is on the exact reason string (grep of assertDeliveryException calls), not merely 'an exception'.

RequestCoreTo never uses nats.Conn.Request, so ErrNoResponders cannot appear; a deaf subject is indistinguishable from a slow one at the listener and both are receipt_timeout by design of the parent contract.

Test wall time for the first test in a go test process includes the shared nats:2.10 testcontainer's creation; Docker on this box took between ~1s and ~42s for that step across runs. The receipt_timeout tests' bodies are ~3s each, bounded by the 2s roleReceiptTimeout.
The workspace working copy carries an untracked-on-main .omp/config.yml; every commit in this phase is path-scoped with jj split so it never lands on the branch.
